prompt:
SOURCE-CORRECTION AND FOUR-POSE PRODUCTION OVERRIDE: Ref1 is a diagnostic source board with precisely FOUR distinct animation layer fragments arranged 2 by 2, not the final eight-slot sheet. Paint only these four shapes, matching their exact visible contours, angles, shading regions and alpha cutouts. Top left cel1920 is276x244 at(80,80); top right1921 is356x220 at(720,80); bottom left1922 is336x284 at(80,530); bottom right1923 is296x312 at(720,530). These are pieces of ONE opaque purple eggplant with a small green calyx, partly occluded by a separate Sam hand layer. The cyan notches on the LEFT are genuine transparent hand/finger occlusion slots, NOT bites, mouths, eyes, fruit flesh, claws or a creature. Preserve their exact outlines and leave them transparent. Do not draw Sam or his hand. Do not fill the missing front side of the fruit. The last pose has two broad rounded left-side cutouts. Ref2 is the already controlled newly painted eggplant/Sam pose and is ONLY a fruit color/line-style reference; no Sam body goes into this output. Ref3 is the approved game inking anchor. Use saturated purple, deep plum shadow, restrained violet highlight on the left, a small crisp green calyx. Preserve the original dark-purple majority shadow in these turned-away poses; do not add a white highlight. Smooth clean hand-inked contours, flat colors with one or two shade shapes, real alpha outside and inside the hand notches. No background, ground, shadow, labels, panels, dots or other objects. We will place each generated layer at fixed4x and copy only exact whole source aliases into the final eight-slot sheets. The protected prompt below is preserved verbatim but its mistaken orange-swirl description, eight-frame layout and final sheet geometry are superseded by this exact four-pose source clarification.

Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat cyan background (#00C8C8). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: a big orange swirl with a purple eggplant. The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (8 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 220 to 312 pixels tall and from 276 to 356 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig347_01/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.
